name: Kadara
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 8 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Blench, Roger. 2009. The Eda [= Kadara] language of Central Nigeria [Eda-English-Hausa wordlist]. Draft circulated for comment, printout July 5, 2009. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. 16 pp. (based on the speech of Alex Maikarfi, Eda/Ada dialect, Adunu area, Niger State). Read from the Internet Archive copy ofhttps://www.rogerblench.info/Language/Niger-Congo/BC/Plateau/Northwest/Eda-English-Hausa%20wordlist.pdf
catalog_locator: sec. 3.3 'Tones', p. 4; prenasalised-consonant remark sec. 3.2, p. 3
catalog_quote: 3.3 Tones Eda has three level tones and both rising and falling tones. The basic conventions used in this list are as follows; High ʹ Mid Unmarked Low ˋ Rising Low-High ˇ Rising Low-Mid ... Rising Mid-High ... Falling High-Low ˆ Falling High-Mid ... Falling Mid-Low ... Eda has undergone significant reduction in a recent period and the proliferation of glide tones is likely to reflect these processes. [p. 3, on homorganic nasal + consonant sequences:] With a very few exceptions, these are not tonebearing.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.citation: one of the works listed for this language (see the verification note)
new_statements.check: reported on verification, not yet confirmed
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Spot-check of the silent/not-opened material: (1) the 2024 revision could not be opened, so nothing can be reported from it; (2) the other Kadara sources already held by the project in the same folder (Blench 2009 Eda wordlist, Hon et al. 2018 SILESR 2018-004, Hon et al. 2012 summary) also give 0 hits for stress/accent/prominence; Blench 2009 sec. 3.3 p. 4 'Eda has three level tones and both rising and falling tones' remains the only prosodic statement. Nothing missed.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. Northwest Plateau materials web page (index of Eda, Ehwa, Ejegha, Kulu, Kuturmi wordlists), rogerblench.info, Internet Archive copy 2024-02-29.
sources.note: Index page only; the Eda wordlist is the sole Kadara item.

sources.citation: OLAC resources for Adara [kad] (language-archives.org, Jan 2026 snapshot) and SIL Language & Culture Archives listing for kad (2015 snapshot).
sources.note: Catalogue only: PARADISEC RB5 audio (Maikarfi 2011 Eda texts/wordlists; Magnusson 2011 Adara), nine SIL 2011 audio wordlists, SIL 2012 summary, SIL 2018 survey. No description with prosody listed.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Christina Riepe & Longdi Sylvanus. 2024. A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Ejuele (Doka) [dbi] Language of Kaduna State, Nigeria, with Notes on Ikulu. Journal of Language Survey Reports. Dallas: SIL International. 68 pp. (2022 version 63 pp.)
sources.note: Glottolog cites pp. 20-22 for the Kadara cluster; recent SIL Nigeria surveys include short phonological observations and retranscribed Kadara-cluster wordlists; low chance of a stress remark.

sources.citation: Ambatu, Solomon Dantawaye. 2021. A contrastive study of English and Adara tenses and aspects: a case of Ewa dialect. MA thesis, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria. 274 pp.
sources.note: No word-stress statement for Adara ('stress' only about English auxiliaries). Summarises Blench 2009 segment inventory, calls Adara 'a tone language', notes tone marks plurality, determiners and interrogatives. Ewa = Ekhwa dialect (ISO ikv), not kad proper.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2018. Nominal affixes and number marking in the Plateau languages of Central Nigeria. In John R. Watters (ed.), East Benue-Congo: Nouns, pronouns, and verbs, 107-172. Berlin: Language Science Press.
sources.note: p.118 mentions Eda [=Kadara] dialect survey, preliminary alphabet book and 2009 alphabet chart; noun-class morphology only; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Hon, Luther, Grace Ajaegbu, Carol Magnusson, Uche S. Nweke & Zachariah Yoder. 2018. A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Adara of Kaduna and Niger States, Nigeria. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2018-004. Dallas: SIL International. 78 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic survey with IPA wordlists of five varieties (Adara, Ada, Eneje, Ajiya, Ekhwa), no phonology, no tone or stress statement.

sources.citation: Hon, Luther, Grace Ajaegbu, Carol Magnusson, Uche S. Nweke & Zachariah Yoder. 2012. A Summary of a Sociolinguistic Survey of the Adara of Kaduna and Niger States, Nigeria. Jos: Language Development Facilitators (SIL Nigeria), 27 April 2012. 21 pp.

Blench, Roger. 2009. The Eda [= Kadara] language of Central Nigeria [Eda-English-Hausa wordlist]. Draft circulated for comment, printout July 5, 2009. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. 16 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent (0 hits). Sec. 3.3 Tones (p.4): 'Eda has three level tones and both rising and falling tones.' plus tone-marking conventions; sec. 3.1-3.2 vowels (7, residual ATR harmony) and consonants.
